title: Weighted Fourier bound for the twisted lift of a far-from-linear function
statement:
Let $p$ be prime and let $f : \bbz_p^n \to \bbz_p$ be normalized, meaning $f(0) = 0$, and $\varepsilon$-far from linear: $0 \le \varepsilon \le 1$ and $\mathrm{dist}(f,g) \ge \varepsilon$ for every linear function $g : \bbz_p^n \to \bbz_p$, where $\mathrm{dist}$ denotes the fraction of inputs on which the two functions disagree. Fix a nonzero $j \in \bbz_p$ and let $\widetilde{f}_j(x) = \omega_p^{\,j\, f(x)}$ be the associated $j$-twisted lift, with $\omega_p = e^{2\pi i / p}$, and write $\widehat{\widetilde{f}_j}(s)$ for its Fourier coefficient at frequency $s$. Then
\[
  \sum_{s \in \bbz_p^n} \bigl|\widehat{\widetilde{f}_j}(s)\bigr|^2 \,\operatorname{Re}\widehat{\widetilde{f}_j}(s)
  \;\le\; 1 - \bigl(1 - \cos(2\pi/p)\bigr)\varepsilon .
\]
hypotheses_covered: f is ε-far from every linear function
replaced:
If $f : \mathbb{Z}_p^n \to \mathbb{Z}_p$ is $\varepsilon$-far from linear
(normalized) and $j \ne 0$, then
\[
  \sum_{s\in\mathbb{Z}_p^n}
  \bigl\|\widehat{(\widetilde{f}_j)}(s)\bigr\|^2\,
  \operatorname{Re}\!\left[\widehat{(\widetilde{f}_j)}(s)\right]
  \;\le\; 1 - \bigl(1-\cos(2\pi/p)\bigr)\varepsilon.
\]
